    <div class="grid who">
      <div>
        <p class="eyebrow">The Proposal</p>
        <h2 class="h-lg" id="who-title">A steady foundation for American government</h2>
        <p class="intro">The rules for the people who run the government should not change with every election.</p>
        <p>The charter proposes a <strong>fourth, bureaucratic branch</strong> beside Congress, the executive and the courts. It would research national issues, debate them in a House-style chamber and send its proposals to Congress, which keeps the final say.</p>
        <p>Its members would be <strong>nominated by the states and confirmed by the courts</strong>, bound by an oath of neutrality and recorded by name on every vote.</p>
        <dl class="stats3">
          <div><dt>740</dt><dd>Members</dd></div>
          <div><dt>51</dt><dd>Jurisdictions</dd></div>
          <div><dt>5</dt><dd>Departments</dd></div>
        </dl>

<!-- ================= PROPOSAL ================= -->
<div data-page="proposal" hidden>
  <header class="page-head">
    <img class="ph-img ph-proposal" src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="" decoding="async" loading="lazy">
    <div class="grid">
      <p class="crumb"><a href="#home">Home</a><span aria-hidden="true">/</span><span>The Proposal</span></p>
      <p class="eyebrow">The Proposal</p>
      <h1 class="h-xl">A fourth branch, built for continuity</h1>
      <p class="dek">The National Advisory &amp; Discussion Commission would research national issues, debate them in the open and send its proposals to Congress.</p>
    </div>
  </header>

  <section class="section" aria-labelledby="glance-title">
    <div class="grid">
      <div class="sec-head"><p class="eyebrow">At a glance</p><h2 class="h-lg" id="glance-title">What the charter establishes</h2></div>
      <div class="cols3">
        <div class="col"><span class="no">01</span><h3 class="h-md">What it is</h3><p>A permanent, nonpartisan body of 740 members, established by constitutional amendment as an assisting branch of government.</p><a class="src" href="#article-ii-principles-of-the-nadc">Article II, Section 1</a></div>
        <div class="col"><span class="no">02</span><h3 class="h-md">Who serves</h3><p>Politically neutral experts. State supreme courts prepare the lists, the states nominate and the judiciary confirms.</p><a class="src" href="#article-iii-representation-process-by-state">Article III</a></div>
        <div class="col"><span class="no">03</span><h3 class="h-md">How it acts</h3><p>Members debate and vote by name. Approved proposals go to Congress as NADC bills and must be authorized there to become law.</p><a class="src" href="#article-v-proposition-proceedings-and-voting">Articles II and V</a></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section class="section soft" aria-labelledby="why-title">
    <div class="grid split">
      <div><p class="eyebrow">Why now</p><h2 class="h-lg" id="why-title">Stability for the civil service</h2></div>
      <div>
        <p class="big">The Office of Personnel Management has finalized “Schedule Policy/Career,” which allows up to 50,000 career employees in policy-influencing roles to be moved into an at-will category.</p>
        <p>The charter holds that the rules governing the people who run the government should not change with each administration. A permanent, neutral Commission would give that system stable footing.</p>
        <a class="textlink" href="#statement-of-purpose">Read the Statement of Purpose <span aria-hidden="true">→</span></a>
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section class="section" aria-labelledby="principles-title">
    <div class="grid">
      <div class="sec-head"><p class="eyebrow">Principles</p><h2 class="h-lg" id="principles-title">Three commitments</h2></div>
      <div class="cols3">
        <div class="col"><h3 class="h-md">Neutral</h3><p>Clause I, “Fixation on Neutrality,” bars political bending and biased decision-making of any kind.</p><a class="src" href="#article-ii-principles-of-the-nadc">Article II, Section 2</a></div>
        <div class="col"><h3 class="h-md">Researched</h3><p>Every proposition arrives with a statement of purpose and its research, then goes to the relevant department for review.</p><a class="src" href="#article-v-proposition-proceedings-and-voting">Article V, Sections 1 and 2</a></div>
        <div class="col"><h3 class="h-md">Accountable</h3><p>Every vote is recorded by name, and debates and votes are published within seven days.</p><a class="src" href="#article-v-proposition-proceedings-and-voting">Article V, Section 5</a></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section class="section soft" aria-labelledby="branches-title">

<!-- ================= FOUNDATIONS ================= -->
<div data-page="foundations" hidden>
  <header class="page-head">
    <img class="ph-img ph-foundations" src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="" decoding="async" loading="lazy">
    <div class="grid">
      <p class="crumb"><a href="#home">Home</a><span aria-hidden="true">/</span><span>Foundations</span></p>
      <p class="eyebrow">Foundations</p>
      <h1 class="h-xl">The reforms that came before</h1>
      <p class="dek">This proposal draws on two earlier efforts to build a professional, accountable federal government: the civil service reforms of President Jimmy Carter and the reinvention work led by Vice President Al Gore.</p>
    </div>
  </header>

  <div class="disclaim"><div class="grid"><p>Neither Jimmy Carter nor Al Gore endorsed this proposal or is connected to it. Their work is described here as historical background and inspiration.</p></div></div>

  <section class="section" aria-labelledby="carter-title">
    <div class="grid figure-row">
      <figure class="portrait">
        <img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="720" height="893" alt="Jimmy Carter speaking at a podium, in a black and white photograph" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
        <figcaption>Jimmy Carter, 39th President of the United States, 1977 to 1981</figcaption>
      </figure>
      <div class="figure-text">
        <p class="eyebrow">1978 · Civil Service Reform Act</p>
        <h2 class="h-lg" id="carter-title">Jimmy Carter and the merit system</h2>
        <p class="big">President Carter made reform of the federal civil service a central goal of his administration. The Civil Service Reform Act of 1978 replaced the Civil Service Commission, which had overseen federal hiring since 1883, with institutions that still serve today.</p>
        <dl class="reforms">
          <div><dt>Office of Personnel Management</dt><dd>Manages the federal workforce and its personnel rules.</dd></div>
          <div><dt>Merit Systems Protection Board</dt><dd>Hears employee appeals and safeguards the merit system.</dd></div>
          <div><dt>Federal Labor Relations Authority</dt><dd>Oversees labor relations across federal agencies.</dd></div>
          <div><dt>Senior Executive Service</dt><dd>A corps of senior career leaders who run federal programs.</dd></div>
          <div><dt>Whistleblower protections</dt><dd>Merit principles written into law, with protection for employees who report wrongdoing.</dd></div>
        </dl>
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section class="section soft" aria-labelledby="carter-align-title">
    <div class="grid">
      <div class="sec-head"><p class="eyebrow">Carter and the charter</p><h2 class="h-lg" id="carter-align-title">How it shapes this proposal</h2></div>
      <div class="align">
        <div><h3 class="h-md">Protection from party pressure</h3><p>The 1978 reforms were built to keep federal service grounded in merit rather than politics. The charter begins with the same aim: to “protect the machinery of public administration from the changing winds of party and power.” Members may not hold party office or take part in campaigns.</p><a class="src" href="#article-vi-oath-conduct-and-removal-of-members">Preamble and Article VI, Section 2</a></div>
        <div><h3 class="h-md">Merit and qualification</h3><p>Members of the Bureaucrats department must clear an assigned federal or state civil service examination, and once chosen they complete a two-month leadership course in public management.</p><a class="src" href="#article-iv-departments-of-the-nadc">Article IV, Sections 16 and 17</a></div>
        <div><h3 class="h-md">A senior executive corps</h3><p>Carter's Senior Executive Service placed experienced career leaders at the top of federal programs. The charter echoes that idea in the Senior In-Selected Executive, under which defense representatives serve.</p><a class="src" href="#article-iv-departments-of-the-nadc">Article IV, Section 3</a></div>
        <div><h3 class="h-md">The debate today</h3><p>The Office of Personnel Management, created by the 1978 Act, issued the Schedule Policy/Career rule that the Statement of Purpose cites as the reason this Commission is needed now.</p><a class="src" href="#statement-of-purpose">Statement of Purpose</a></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section class="section" aria-labelledby="gore-title">
    <div class="grid figure-row flip">
      <figure class="portrait">
        <img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," width="394" height="493" alt="Al Gore in a suit and tie, with the Capitol dome behind him" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
        <figcaption>Al Gore, 45th Vice President of the United States, 1993 to 2001</figcaption>
      </figure>
      <div class="figure-text">
        <p class="eyebrow">1993 · National Performance Review</p>
        <h2 class="h-lg" id="gore-title">Al Gore and reinventing government</h2>
        <p class="big">In March 1993, President Bill Clinton asked Vice President Gore to lead the National Performance Review, a government-wide examination of how federal agencies do their work.</p>
        <p>Its first report, <em>From Red Tape to Results: Creating a Government That Works Better and Costs Less</em>, followed that September. It called on agencies to cut red tape, put customers first, empower employees to get results and cut back to basics. In 1998 the effort became the National Partnership for Reinventing Government.</p>
        <p>Agencies published customer service standards, and the Vice President's Hammer Award recognized federal teams that made government work better and cost less.</p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section class="section soft" aria-labelledby="gore-align-title">
    <div class="grid">
      <div class="sec-head"><p class="eyebrow">Gore and the charter</p><h2 class="h-lg" id="gore-align-title">How it shapes this proposal</h2></div>
      <div class="align">
        <div><h3 class="h-md">Efficiency as a founding purpose</h3><p>The charter states that the Commission exists because “the government could efficiently use an assisting bureaucratic branch.”</p><a class="src" href="#article-ii-principles-of-the-nadc">Article II, Section 1</a></div>
        <div><h3 class="h-md">Performance and results</h3><p>Terms are limited to three re-commissionings, and the state and the NADC Board allot eligibility based on term performance.</p><a class="src" href="#article-iii-representation-process-by-state">Article III, Section 2</a></div>
        <div><h3 class="h-md">Expertise where it counts</h3><p>Each representative is assigned to a sector based on experience and expertise, and states may assign finance experts who have earned their expertise in the field.</p><a class="src" href="#article-iii-representation-process-by-state">Article III, Section 5 and Article IV, Section 23</a></div>
        <div><h3 class="h-md">Open to the public</h3><p>Every proposition receives a written report within thirty days, every vote is recorded by name, and debates and votes are published within seven days.</p><a class="src" href="#article-v-proposition-proceedings-and-voting">Article V, Sections 2 and 5</a></div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>

  <section class="section" aria-labelledby="shared-title">
    <div class="grid split">
      <div><p class="eyebrow">A shared conviction</p><h2 class="h-lg" id="shared-title">Carrying the idea forward</h2></div>
      <div>
        <p class="big">Both reforms rested on one idea: the people who carry out the work of government should be chosen for skill, held to account for results and shielded from partisan pressure.</p>
        <p>The National Advisory &amp; Discussion Commission is an attempt to carry that idea forward as a permanent branch, fixed in the Constitution so that it does not change with each administration.</p>
        <a class="textlink" href="#charter">Read the charter <span aria-hidden="true">→</span></a>
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>
</div>

<!-- ================= CHARTER ================= -->
<div data-page="charter" hidden>
  <header class="page-head">

      <p class="eyebrow">The Charter</p>
      <h1 class="h-xl">Manifesto and Charter</h1>
      <p class="dek">National Advisory &amp; Discussion Commission, United States Edition. The complete text, with search and a table of contents.</p>
    </div>
  </header>
  <section class="section" aria-label="Charter text" style="padding-top:48px">
    <div class="grid">
      <div class="reader">
        <aside class="sidenav-wrap" aria-label="Charter contents">

<section>
<h2 id="preamble">Preamble</h2>
<p>We, the people of the United States, in order to secure a neutral, researched, and accountable government, to protect the machinery of public administration from the changing winds of party and power, and to guarantee the welfare of the nation and the public, do hereby propose and establish this charter for the National Advisory &amp; Discussion Commission of the United States.</p>
</section>
<section>
<h2 id="statement-of-purpose">Statement of Purpose</h2>
<p>The need for the said Commission stands clearer now than ever before. The Office of Personnel Management has recently finalized "Schedule Policy/Career," a rule under which up to 50,000 career employees in policy-influencing roles may be moved into an at-will category. Its supporters have described the said rule as accountability, whereas its critics have stated that such employees shall lose independent appeals if they believe they have been removed for political reasons. Irrespective of the side one takes, the rules governing the persons who run the government now change each time the White House does. A permanent and neutral Commission would provide the said machinery with stable ground upon which to stand.</p>
</section>
<section>
<h2 id="contents-of-this-charter">Contents of this Charter</h2>
<p>The following manifesto hereby sets out the following aspects of the NADC, as follows:</p>
<ul>
<li>Article I: Establishment of the Commission</li>
<li>Article II: Principles of the NADC</li>
<li>Article III: Representation Process by State</li>
<li>Article IV: Departments of the NADC</li>
<li>Article V: Proposition Proceedings and Voting</li>
<li>Article VI: Oath, Conduct, and Removal of Members</li>
<li>Article VII: Amendment of this Charter</li>
<li>First Schedule: Committee Weightage by State</li>
<li>Second Schedule: Category Distribution by State</li>
</ul>
</section>
<section>
<h2 id="article-i-establishment-of-the-commission">Article I: Establishment of the Commission</h2>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 1.</span> There shall be established within the Government of the United States a new advisory and discussion body, to be known as the National Advisory &amp; Discussion Commission (hereinafter referred to as the "NADC" or the "Commission"). The Commission is hereby proposed after years of propositions and a rising need for a significant and powerful body within governmental authority, and the said authority shall hold significant control in the proceedings of the federal government.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 2.</span> The members of the Commission shall be selected through criteria which shall differ with the background from which they come. In the selection process, each state shall be allotted a set number of representatives, based on the different criteria and preferences laid down in Article III. The states shall nominate the said representatives, and the judiciary shall confirm them.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 3.</span> The implementation of law within the Commission shall not differ from the regular enforcement of law in any other federal body. The purpose of the Commission is to make government decision-making more bureaucratic, more democratic, and better researched and analyzed. The Congress of the United States shall be legally permitted to criticize and condemn the decisions of the Commission.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 4.</span> The Commission shall ensure that only politically neutral and intellectual members are given a chance to represent the states and sectors. Outside of the fifty states, representation shall be allotted to Washington, D.C. alone.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 5.</span> The Commission shall democratically vote upon the decisions and propositions brought before it, and shall follow a traditional parliamentary-style debate format, with the same manner of seating, debate, and representation as the House of Representatives of the United States.</p>
</section>
<section>
<h2 id="article-ii-principles-of-the-nadc">Article II: Principles of the NADC</h2>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 1.</span> The Commission has been set up because the government could efficiently use an assisting bureaucratic branch. The Commission shall be permanently ratified into the Constitution of the United States by way of amendment, thereby fixing it for all future governments permanently.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 2.</span> Clause I of the Commission has been identified as "Fixation on Neutrality," which shall prohibit the Commission from political bending and biased decision-making of any kind.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 3.</span> The Commission is also established upon the principle of self-government, guaranteeing the welfare of the nation and the public, in accordance with the promise of the Constitution to "promote the general Welfare."</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 4.</span> The selection criteria of the Commission shall be such as to efficiently reach only the right representatives. Representatives who are a part of the Commission shall be permanently relieved from all other public services, and any member who abuses the said position shall be subject to a dishonorable discharge from all national service.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 5.</span> The NADC shall discuss and analyze the various national elements and issues, and the members of the Commission shall be more than qualified to vote and decide upon such topics. The Commission shall remain neutral towards religion, race, background, party, or even state.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 6.</span> The Commission has been formed to bring the justice which both the government and the people of the country deserve. Regardless of the political party to which they belong, governments have always taken enforcing actions which have damaged the integrity and intellect of the government. With the formation of the National Advisory &amp; Discussion Commission, democracy and bureaucracy shall gain a new representation, and better insight and involvement in public decision-making.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 7.</span> All the decisions ratified by the Commission shall go through the regular bill process of the Congress and be authorized legally. The bills ratified or proposed by the Commission shall fall under the "NADC" category of bills, which is hereby created solely for the bills proposed by the Commission.</p>
</section>
<section>
<h2 id="article-iii-representation-process-by-state">Article III: Representation Process by State</h2>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 1.</span> The NADC shall choose candidates who fit the eligibility criteria laid down hereunder. The number of representatives of each state shall be determined by a list of factors for the said state, and shall follow the exact amount as prescribed by the NADC Board. The number of representatives shall be determined by the following:</p>
<p><strong>(a) Population.</strong> Population shall play a major role in deciding the number of representatives allotted to a state, and the said criterion shall account for 47% of the total requirement. Low-population states shall be given three subsidiary seats in order to reduce the population representation inequality in the NADC. The way and process of measuring each state's population and recording it for representational purposes shall be allotted to the United States Census Bureau, and shall be measured in the same way as it is for the apportionment of seats in the House of Representatives.</p>
<p><strong>(b) GDP.</strong> Population shall not be the sole factor in determining the number of representatives. The economic performance of a state, as measured by the Bureau of Economic Analysis, shall also play a significant role in the process, and the said criterion shall account for 20% of the selected representatives of a state. This criterion is added to reward and keep the financial and economic contributions of a state into account, and it is the criterion which differs from a traditional representation process. The maximum number of seats which may be assigned under this criterion shall be 13, so that performing well as a state in economic aspects may be rewarded by means of representation.</p>
<p><strong>(c) GDP per capita.</strong> Each state shall also gain a few more selected representatives in the Commission based on its GDP per capita. This criterion has been mentioned and listed to reflect and reward each state for its work towards improving the quality of life of its citizens. The maximum number of seats which may be gained under this criterion shall be 3. The GDP per capita shall be updated as per the seat allocation requirement of the Commission. Under this criterion, a state may be allotted seats only for three consecutive terms before being relieved for three terms, which shall create a fundamental balance in the seat allotment procedure. The state shall still be subject to a reduction of members during the relief period.</p>
<p><strong>(d) Education.</strong> One of the most crucial elements in the allocation of state representatives shall be the education rate of the state, as measured by the American Community Survey of the Census Bureau. The education rate of a state reflects upon how educated and informed its citizens are, and their contribution towards the growth of the state and the nation. An educated state also reflects how much initiative the state government has taken to improve it. States shall be allotted additional representatives based on their performance, and the maximum number of representatives which may be allotted to a state under this criterion shall be 8. A re-counting of the education rate of the state shall be done every four years, so as to ensure the supplements of a state government's initiatives.</p>
<p><strong>(e) Historical and cultural significance.</strong> Even though every state has its own unique significance towards the national history, some states shall be granted a supplementary number of representatives based on their significance. The top ten states in the country falling under this criterion shall be given the additional representatives, and the maximum allotment under this criterion shall be 4 more representational members. This criterion is added within the portfolio in order to achieve the mission of granting historically dedicated states more representation.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 2.</span> The aforesaid criteria shall be set up by the Supreme Court of the United States, keeping in view all the different strengths of the different states. Each state shall be allotted a set number of representational members. The terms of the representatives shall be limited to three re-commissionings, with a term of three to four years each. The state and the NADC Board shall allot eligibility based upon term performance.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 3.</span> A representative may represent three different states in three different elections. Clause III of the constitution of the Commission states that a person may run for re-election up to five times if the said representative has changed states three times, thereby ensuring a fair representation time to each state.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 4.</span> The states shall have to make a new list of representatives every three elections for re-organization, and shall then submit the list of representatives who shall get a chance to represent them. The supreme courts of the individual states are hereby allotted the authority to prepare the state-wise list of all the state representatives. If the name of a candidate is repeated, the states shall negotiate with each other and resolve the conflict. Every state shall be required to have at least 25% backup or optional representatives.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 5.</span> The main responsibility of the representatives shall be to represent these top priorities:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Welfare of the common American citizen.</strong> The representatives of the NADC are chosen by the judiciary to firstly prioritize and play a significant role in the proposition of designated bills and laws, which are well argued and researched in the Commission.</li>
<li><strong>Contributing to the allotted sector.</strong> Each representative shall be assigned a public sector based upon his or her previous experience and expertise, so as to make the said representative efficient in the role of representation. If a representative is assigned the defense sector, the same shall be the sole assigned area of representation.</li>
</ul>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 6.</span> The session of the NADC shall be distributed among the following sectors, as follows:</p>
<div class="tablewrap"><table class=""><thead><tr><th><strong>Sector</strong></th><th><strong>Share of the session</strong></th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Defense</td><td>25% to 45%</td></tr><tr><td>Finance</td><td>5% to 30%</td></tr><tr><td>Diplomacy</td><td>2% to 17%</td></tr><tr><td>Law</td><td>5% to 35%</td></tr></tbody></table></div>
</section>
<section>
<h2 id="article-iv-departments-of-the-nadc">Article IV: Departments of the NADC</h2>
<h3 id="part-a-defense">Part A: Defense</h3>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 1.</span> The defensive structure of a country is built upon national unity, but often ignored is the state-level contribution towards defense. Each state has been allotted a set number of defense representatives, based upon the population of the state and its preference. The said defense representatives shall work with the Department of Defense and the military branches themselves, and shall promote their ecosystems within the state.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 2.</span> The defense representatives shall also be responsible for bringing military industry into their home state, and shall advocate for a more politically secure defense sector within their state. They shall also oversee the progress of the military trend in their state, that is:</p>
<ul>
<li>Enlistment statistics</li>
<li>Military industry</li>
<li>Foreign industrial establishments</li>
<li>The financial record of the military forces of their state</li>
</ul>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 3.</span> States which border a different country shall be provided with one default representative. The defense representatives may be chosen from any default number or background of representatives. The selected Class B payment salary chart shall apply, and their jurisdiction shall come under the Senior In-Selected Executive.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 4.</span> In order to bring an order into effect, the representative shall have to obtain a finalized clearance from the head of the committee. Each qualified defense representative shall be allotted an official passport during the term of service, with strict regulations. All expenses, from housing to travelling, shall be borne by the Government of the United States.</p>
<h3 id="part-b-department-allocation-for-defense">Part B: Department Allocation for Defense</h3>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 5.</span> Defense plays a crucial role in the protection of a country, and defense is one of the allotted sectors in the Commission. A state shall have a full-pledged right over the number of defense representatives it wishes to delegate towards the said sector, including a state which wishes most of its state-wise delegation to go towards defense. States which face threat from foreign aggression, or play a significant role in the defense policy of the nation, shall have the total right to send delegates.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 6.</span> Keeping all the different criteria in mind, no state shall have the constitutional right to allocate more than 43% of its representatives towards defense, save and except a state facing a direct security threat, as determined by the NADC Board. This minor clause has been added to the constitution in order to keep the different powers and sectors in checks and stability.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 7.</span> The representatives allotted the defense sector shall be required to have at least eight months of defense contribution to the nation. This shall help keep a balance, clear out the unbelonging candidates, and create a more professional and experienced branch. The NADC authority is hereby given the charge to make sure that no politically or ideologically sided or biased candidate is selected for the sector. Representatives who have served under the defense sector shall be eligible for a fourth re-election in times of war or national emergency.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 8.</span> Any evidence of forging or fraud against the NADC shall result in expulsion from the Commission and a trial in the Supreme Court. If found guilty, the accused shall be dishonorably discharged from all present and future government benefits.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 9.</span> The transferring process towards the Commission shall take place over a two-month election cycle. Firstly, an application for slot re-allotment from the individual has to be published. Thereafter, an elected committee of nine shall examine the process and vote. The temporary transfer clause shall allow a temporary department allocation ranging from three weeks to three months.</p>
<h3 id="part-c-public-sector">Part C: Public Sector</h3>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 10.</span> Each state shall also be allotted a set number of representatives towards the public sector. The public sector of a nation is one of the most necessary facilities required to accomplish a well-established public life. The public sector shall include the following daily factors:</p>
<ul>
<li>Healthcare</li>
<li>Transportation</li>
<li>Infrastructure</li>
<li>Schools</li>
<li>Libraries</li>
<li>Religious institutions</li>
<li>Cultural heritage</li>
<li>Economic build-up and industry</li>
<li>Bureaucratic resources</li>
</ul>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 11.</span> Each state shall be allotted public sector representatives based upon its ranking and preference. The said representatives shall divide a specific department for every sector listed above. The number of assistants allocated to all of these sectors shall be 31, which shall then be independently allocated to the selected services. The head representatives shall then take all the suggestions and remarks, and send the most beneficial ones to the head department for approval, so as to put them into effect.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 12.</span> The public sector department shall be allocated the largest share of monetary funds every year. The prime responsibility of this department shall be to create a better developmental flow in all of these sectors. From new school desks to hospital masks, every public facility shall be provided a neutral chance to grow. The state head representative shall be committed under the head of the NADC committee. Second-grade pay shall be given to the top representatives, while third-level pay grade shall be given to the sectional assistants.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 13.</span> A special committee group for this department shall also be established, consisting of:</p>
<ul>
<li>The county executive</li>
<li>The allocated representative</li>
<li>The assistant sectional representatives</li>
<li>The public fundamental officer</li>
<li>Other regional officials</li>
</ul>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 14.</span> The said committee shall specifically oversee the progress of the public sector, the new establishments, and the upcoming projects of the sector. The county executive and the regional officials shall receive an extra stipend of 25% extra salary and 33% extra retirement benefits, provided they have been members of this committee for at least seven years. This department is the only one which may be held as a responsibility towards the county executive, and some other county responsibilities may also be posted upon the representatives of this department by the county executive.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 15.</span> The representatives with a minimum service period of two years in this department shall be given a 35% benefit boost. An inquiry commission which is set upon the representatives of this department may only be removed by the Governor of the state. More detailed rules and regulations shall be brought accordingly.</p>
<h3 id="part-d-bureaucrats">Part D: Bureaucrats</h3>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 16.</span> Each state deserves its own set number of national and international representatives. Their primary assigned responsibility shall be to represent the state in financial, political, diplomatic, regular, industrial, cultural, human rights, judicial, and state electoral conferences. The selection criteria for this department shall be the following regulations:</p>
<ul>
<li>Belong to the state which you are representing</li>
<li>Be a resident of the said state for at least seventeen years</li>
<li>Clear the specifically assigned federal or state civil service examination</li>
<li>Be of the minimum age of at least twenty-eight years</li>
</ul>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 17.</span> The chosen bureaucrats shall go through a two-month-long leadership course in public management, state politics, and other factors. The said bureaucrats shall also have the jurisdiction to bring business and industry into their state, in order to grow it financially. They shall also play key management roles during the state, regional, and legislative elections. Diplomatic scenarios, such as public representation and emergency representation, shall also be assigned to the said representatives.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 18.</span> Regular conferences shall be held with the regional police officials, judges, and civil servants, so as to keep a better flow of public service and administration, and to keep track of regular industrial growth at both the rural and urban level of the assigned region. The bureaucrats shall supervise cultural heritage and maintain religious neutrality at all costs. Any report of human rights misconduct shall also be a public representation event, and shall hence be regulated by the assigned representatives. Any law enforcement branch shall also be a side priority of the chosen representative. The maintaining of healthy and neutral state electoral reforms shall be supervised by a joint interstate representatives meeting.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 19.</span> The bureaucrats shall also be responsible for covering the main progressive state representation on national and international platforms. The state bureaucrats are expected to take charge of the welfare programs of a region, if so assigned. The bureaucrats shall be assigned at the B-level pay grade, with local members being placed at the C-level.</p>
<h3 id="part-e-law-and-regulation">Part E: Law and Regulation</h3>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 20.</span> The regulatory and constitutional laws of a country are what define its states as well. The NADC has placed together a department dedicated to better establish the implementation, representation, and regulation of the laws taking place. The Law and Regulation representatives are assigned full or partial contribution in the following constitutional and judicial aspects:</p>
<ul>
<li>Implementation of law within the regularly assigned region</li>
<li>Maintaining judicial enforcement within the courts of the region</li>
<li>Regulation of the laws in a constitutional manner</li>
<li>Helping the regional judicial in-charge in judicial enforcement</li>
</ul>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 21.</span> Each representative shall be assigned a specific aspect in the lawmaking body of the region, and each representative shall be granted two lawyers and thirteen enforcement associates. The regional court district has to abide by the rules of the Law and Regulation department of the NADC. There shall be a committee formed in every region, consisting of the following members:</p>
<ul>
<li>Assistant law enforcement officer</li>
<li>Chief election officer (if invited)</li>
<li>Two district judges</li>
<li>Ten district-recognized lawyers</li>
<li>The elected member of Congress of the region</li>
</ul>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 22.</span> In case of instability or unrest in the region, a special law and power may be enacted as per the regulatory body of the NADC.</p>
<h3 id="part-f-finance">Part F: Finance</h3>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 23.</span> Finance is a very crucial and significant part of the NADC body. Each state has been given a preference on whether it would like to assign to itself finance ministry experts, who have gained their expertise in the field.</p>
</section>
<section>
<h2 id="article-v-proposition-proceedings-and-voting">Article V: Proposition Proceedings and Voting</h2>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 1.</span> Any proposition before the Commission may be introduced by a representative, by a department of the Commission, or by a reference from the Congress of the United States. Every proposition shall be submitted in writing to the NADC Board, along with a statement of its purpose and the research upon which it is based.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 2.</span> Every proposition shall first be examined by the department under whose sector it falls. The said department shall study the proposition for a period not exceeding thirty days, and shall return it to the full Commission with a written report and its recommendation.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 3.</span> No proposition shall be voted upon unless at least one-half of the total members of the Commission are present, which shall constitute the quorum. Each representative shall have one vote, and no vote shall be cast by proxy.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 4.</span> A proposition shall be passed by a simple majority of the members present and voting. Provided that any proposition relating to defense, to the removal of a member, or to the amendment of this Charter shall require a majority of two-thirds of the members present and voting.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 5.</span> Every vote of the Commission shall be recorded by name, and the record of the debates and votes shall be published for the public within seven days of the said vote, save and except matters which have been declared classified for reasons of national security by the NADC Board.</p>
</section>
<section>
<h2 id="article-vi-oath-conduct-and-removal-of-members">Article VI: Oath, Conduct, and Removal of Members</h2>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 1.</span> Every representative shall, before entering upon the office, take the following oath: "I do solemnly swear (or affirm) that I will bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of the United States and to this Charter, that I will remain neutral in all matters before the Commission, and that I will faithfully discharge the duties of my office for the welfare of the people."</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 2.</span> No representative shall, during the term of service, hold any office in a political party, take part in the campaign of any candidate for public office, or receive any gift, payment, or benefit from any person or organization having an interest in the matters before the Commission.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 3.</span> Every representative shall disclose all financial interests to the NADC Board at the beginning of each term, and shall recuse himself or herself from any proposition in which he or she holds a personal or financial interest.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 4.</span> A representative may be removed from office for proven misconduct, partisan conduct, or incapacity. The proceedings of removal shall be initiated by the NADC Board or by a petition signed by one-fourth of the members of the Commission, shall be inquired into by the supreme court of the state of the said representative, and shall require a vote of two-thirds of the members present and voting. A representative removed under this Section shall be replaced from the backup list of his or her state, as provided in Article III.</p>
</section>
<section>
<h2 id="article-vii-amendment-of-this-charter">Article VII: Amendment of this Charter</h2>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 1.</span> An amendment to this Charter may be proposed by the NADC Board, by one-third of the members of the Commission, or by a resolution of the Congress of the United States.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 2.</span> Any proposed amendment shall be passed by a majority of two-thirds of the members of the Commission present and voting, and shall thereafter be laid before the Congress, which may reject the same within ninety days. If the Congress does not reject the said amendment within the said period, it shall come into force.</p>
<p class="clause"><span class="secno">Section 3.</span> Provided that no amendment shall alter Clause I, "Fixation on Neutrality," or reduce the representation of any state below the minimum laid down in Article III, unless the same is ratified by the legislatures of three-fourths of the several states.</p>
</section>
<section>
<h2 id="schedules-seat-distribution-by-state">Schedules: Seat Distribution by State</h2>
<p>In accordance with the criteria laid down in Article III, the Commission shall seat 740 members from the fifty states and Washington, D.C. Population shall account for close to one-half of all the seats and GDP for about one-fifth, with the remainder being allotted under the GDP per capita, education, historical significance, and low-population criteria. Population shall be measured by the apportionment count of the Census Bureau, GDP and GDP per capita by the Bureau of Economic Analysis, and education by the share of adults with a bachelor's degree or higher in the American Community Survey. Every state shall receive at least two population seats.</p>
<p>The additional seats shall be given as follows:</p>
<ul>
<li>GDP per capita: +3 at $100,000 or more, +2 at $90,000 or more, +1 at $85,000 or more</li>
<li>Education: +8 at 42% or more with a bachelor's degree, +7 at 39%, +6 at 37%, +5 at 35%</li>
<li>Historical and cultural significance: up to +4 for the top ten states</li>
<li>Low-population states (under 1.5 million people): +3 subsidiary seats</li>
</ul>
</section>

<section>
<h2 id="second-schedule-category-distribution-by-state">Second Schedule: Category Distribution by State</h2>
<p>The seats of each state shall be divided among the five departments in the same proportions as the original model. States which border a different country shall retain at least one defense representative, and no state shall exceed the limit of 43% towards defense laid down in Article IV.</p>

<!-- ================= FAQ ================= -->
<div data-page="faq" hidden>
  <header class="page-head">
    <img class="ph-img ph-faq" src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="" decoding="async" loading="lazy">
    <div class="grid">
      <p class="crumb"><a href="#home">Home</a><span aria-hidden="true">/</span><span>FAQ</span></p>
      <p class="eyebrow">FAQ</p>
      <h1 class="h-xl">Questions and answers</h1>
      <p class="dek">Plain-language answers to common questions. Each one points to the part of the charter that governs it.</p>
    </div>
  </header>
  <section class="section" aria-label="Frequently asked questions">
    <div class="grid">
      <div class="faq-tools"><button class="btn btn-outline btn-sm" id="faqAll" type="button">Expand all</button></div>
      <div class="accordion faq">
      <details><summary>Is the Commission a government agency?</summary>
        <p>No. The Commission is a proposal. It would be established only through an amendment to the U.S. Constitution (<a href="#article-ii-principles-of-the-nadc">Article II, Section 1</a>).</p></details>

      <details><summary>Would it replace Congress?</summary>
        <p>No. Every decision the Commission approves must pass through the regular legislative process and be authorized by Congress (<a href="#article-ii-principles-of-the-nadc">Article II, Section 7</a>). Congress may also criticize the Commission's decisions (<a href="#article-i-establishment-of-the-commission">Article I, Section 3</a>) and reject amendments to its charter within ninety days (<a href="#article-vii-amendment-of-this-charter">Article VII, Section 2</a>).</p></details>

      <details><summary>What would the Commission do?</summary>
        <p>It researches, debates and votes on national issues, then sends its proposals to Congress as a new category of NADC bills. Its members serve in five departments: defense, public sector, bureaucrats, law and regulation, and finance (<a href="#article-iv-departments-of-the-nadc">Articles II and IV</a>).</p></details>

      <details><summary>Why is it needed now?</summary>
        <p>In 2026, the Office of Personnel Management finalized "Schedule Policy/Career," which allows up to 50,000 career employees in policy-influencing roles to be moved into an at-will category. The charter holds that the rules governing the civil service should not change with each administration, and that a permanent, neutral Commission would give the system stable footing (<a href="#statement-of-purpose">Statement of Purpose</a>).</p></details>

      <details><summary>How are members chosen?</summary>
        <p>Members are not elected. Each state's supreme court prepares a list of representatives, the state nominates them and the judiciary confirms them. Every state also maintains a backup list of at least 25 percent (<a href="#article-iii-representation-process-by-state">Article I, Section 2 and Article III, Section 4</a>).</p></details>

      <details><summary>How does the charter protect neutrality?</summary>
        <p>Neutrality is Clause I of the charter, titled "Fixation on Neutrality." Members swear an oath of neutrality, may not hold party office or campaign, may not accept gifts from interested parties, must disclose their finances and must recuse themselves from any vote in which they hold an interest (<a href="#article-vi-oath-conduct-and-removal-of-members">Article VI</a>). Changing Clause I requires three-fourths of the state legislatures (<a href="#article-vii-amendment-of-this-charter">Article VII, Section 3</a>).</p></details>

      <details><summary>Why do GDP and education affect representation?</summary>
        <p>Population remains the largest factor, accounting for close to half of all seats. The charter also recognizes economic output, GDP per capita, education and historical significance, each within a set cap. Smaller states receive three additional seats so they keep a meaningful voice (<a href="#article-iii-representation-process-by-state">Article III, Section 1</a> and the Schedules).</p></details>

      <details><summary>Why does California hold the most seats?</summary>
        <p>California has the largest population and the largest economy, and it also qualifies for seats based on GDP per capita, education and history. Together, these give it 64 of the 740 seats (<a href="#first-schedule-committee-weightage-by-state">First Schedule</a>).</p></details>

      <details><summary>How does a proposal pass?</summary>
        <p>The relevant department first reviews the proposal for up to thirty days. At least half of all members must then be present, and the proposal passes with a simple majority of those voting. Proposals on defense, the removal of a member or amendments to the charter require a two-thirds vote (<a href="#article-v-proposition-proceedings-and-voting">Article V</a>).</p></details>

      <details><summary>Are votes public?</summary>
        <p>Yes. Every vote is recorded by name, and debates and votes are published within seven days. The only exception is a matter declared classified for national security (<a href="#article-v-proposition-proceedings-and-voting">Article V, Section 5</a>).</p></details>

      <details><summary>Can a member be removed?</summary>
        <p>Yes, for proven misconduct, partisan conduct or incapacity. Removal may be initiated by the NADC Board or by a petition from one-quarter of the members. The member's state supreme court conducts an inquiry, and removal requires a two-thirds vote. A replacement is drawn from the state's backup list (<a href="#article-vi-oath-conduct-and-removal-of-members">Article VI, Section 4</a>).</p></details>

      </div>
    </div>
  </section>

    ["Introduced", "A representative, a department of the Commission, or a reference from Congress introduces the proposition. It goes to the NADC Board in writing, with a statement of its purpose and the research behind it.", "Article V, Section 1"],

  function showStep(i) {
    cur = i;

      '<button type="button" class="btn btn-sm" id="nextStep"' + (i === S.length - 1 ? " disabled" : "") + '>Next step</button></div>';
    $("#prevStep").onclick = function () { if (cur > 0) showStep(cur - 1); };
    $("#nextStep").onclick = function () { if (cur < S.length - 1) showStep(cur + 1); };
  }
  $$("#steps button").forEach(function (b) { b.addEventListener("click", function () { showStep(+b.getAttribute("data-i")); }); });
  showStep(0);

  /* ---------- vote calculator ---------- */
  var TOTAL = 740, QUORUM = 370;
  var present = $("#present"), yes = $("#yes");
  var NOTES = {
    general: ["simple majority", "Passes with a simple majority of members present and voting.", "Article V, Section 4", "v"],
    defense: ["two-thirds", "Defense propositions need two-thirds of members present and voting.", "Article V, Section 4", "v"],
    removal: ["two-thirds", "Removal also needs proven misconduct, partisan conduct or incapacity, and an inquiry by the member's state supreme court.", "Article VI, Section 4", "vi"],
    amend: ["two-thirds", "After passing, the amendment goes to Congress, which may reject it within ninety days. Changing Clause I needs three-fourths of the state legislatures.", "Article VII, Sections 2 and 3", "vii"]
  };
  function calc() {
    var type = ($("input[name=ptype]:checked") || {}).value || "general";
    var p = +present.value;
    yes.max = p; if (+yes.value > p) yes.value = p;
    var y = +yes.value;
    $("#presentOut").textContent = p; $("#yesOut").textContent = y;
    var need = type === "general" ? Math.floor(p / 2) + 1 : Math.ceil(p * 2 / 3);
    var pct = function (n) { return p ? (n / p * 100) : 0; };
    $("#vbYes").style.width = pct(y) + "%";
    $("#vbNeed").style.left = Math.min(100, pct(need)) + "%";
    $("#vbNeed").hidden = p < QUORUM;
    var n = NOTES[type], v = $("#verdict");
    if (p < QUORUM) {
      v.className = "alert error";
      v.innerHTML = "<strong>No quorum</strong>At least " + QUORUM + " of " + TOTAL + " members must be present before any vote." + cite("Article V, Section 3", "v");
      return;
    }
    var ok = y >= need;
    v.className = "alert " + (ok ? "success" : "error");
    v.innerHTML = "<strong>" + (ok ? "Passes" : "Fails") + ": " + y + " in favor, " + (p - y) + " against</strong>" +
      "Needs " + need + " of " + p + " (" + n[0] + "). " + esc(n[1]) + cite(n[2], n[3]);
  }
  [present, yes].forEach(function (el) { el.addEventListener("input", calc); });
  $$("input[name=ptype]").forEach(function (el) { el.addEventListener("change", calc); });
  $("#calc").addEventListener("submit", function (e) { e.preventDefault(); });
  calc();

  /* ---------- seat explorer ---------- */
  function tableOf(id) { var h = document.getElementById(id); return h ? h.parentElement.querySelector("table") : null; }
  function rowsOf(t) {
    return Array.prototype.slice.call(t.tBodies[0].rows).filter(function (r) { return !r.classList.contains("total"); })
      .map(function (r) { return Array.prototype.slice.call(r.cells).map(function (c) { return c.textContent.trim(); }); });
  }
  var CRIT = ["Population", "GDP", "GDP per capita", "Education", "Historical", "Low-population"];
  var DEPT = ["Defense", "Public Sector", "Bureaucrats", "Law & Regulation", "Finance"];
  var COL = ["var(--s1)", "var(--s2)", "var(--s3)", "var(--s4)", "var(--s5)", "var(--s6)"];
  var states = {};
  rowsOf(tableOf("first-schedule-committee-weightage-by-state")).forEach(function (c) {
    states[c[0]] = { name: c[0], crit: c.slice(1, 7).map(function (v) { return +v || 0; }), total: +c[7] || 0, dept: [0, 0, 0, 0, 0] };
  });
  rowsOf(tableOf("second-schedule-category-distribution-by-state")).forEach(function (c) {
    if (states[c[0]]) states[c[0]].dept = c.slice(1, 6).map(function (v) { return +v || 0; });
  });
  var list = Object.keys(states).map(function (k) { return states[k]; });
  var maxTotal = Math.max.apply(null, list.map(function (s) { return s.total; }));
  var critTot = CRIT.map(function (_, i) { return list.reduce(function (a, s) { return a + s.crit[i]; }, 0); });
  var deptTot = DEPT.map(function (_, i) { return list.reduce(function (a, s) { return a + s.dept[i]; }, 0); });
  var grand = list.reduce(function (a, s) { return a + s.total; }, 0);

  function stackHTML(vals, labels, ctx) {
    var sum = vals.reduce(function (a, b) { return a + b; }, 0) || 1;
    return vals.map(function (v, i) { return v ? '<i style="flex:' + v + ' 1 0;background:' + COL[i] + '" data-tip="' + esc(ctx + ": " + labels[i] + ", " + v + " seat" + (v === 1 ? "" : "s") + " (" + (v / sum * 100).toFixed(1) + "%)") + '"></i>' : ""; }).join("");
  }
  function legendHTML(vals, labels) { return vals.map(function (v, i) { return '<li><i style="background:' + COL[i] + '"></i>' + esc(labels[i]) + ' <b>' + v + '</b></li>'; }).join(""); }
  $("#sumCrit").innerHTML = stackHTML(critTot, CRIT, "All states");
  $("#legCrit").innerHTML = legendHTML(critTot, CRIT);
  $("#sumDept").innerHTML = stackHTML(deptTot, DEPT, "All states");
  $("#legDept").innerHTML = legendHTML(deptTot, DEPT);

  var sortOpts = [["total", "Total seats"], ["c0", "Population seats"], ["c1", "GDP seats"], ["c2", "GDP per capita seats"], ["c3", "Education seats"], ["c4", "Historical seats"], ["c5", "Low-population seats"],
    ["d0", "Defense seats"], ["d1", "Public Sector seats"], ["d2", "Bureaucrat seats"], ["d3", "Law & Regulation seats"], ["d4", "Finance seats"], ["az", "Name, A to Z"]];
  $("#sortBy").innerHTML = sortOpts.map(function (o) { return '<option value="' + o[0] + '">' + esc(o[1]) + '</option>'; }).join("");
  var view = "crit", selected = "California";

  function sortVal(s, key) { if (key === "total") return s.total; if (key[0] === "c") return s.crit[+key[1]]; if (key[0] === "d") return s.dept[+key[1]]; return 0; }
  function renderRows() {
    var q = $("#stateSearch").value.trim().toLowerCase(), key = $("#sortBy").value;
    var arr = list.filter(function (s) { return !q || s.name.toLowerCase().indexOf(q) !== -1; });
    arr.sort(function (a, b) { if (key === "az") return a.name.localeCompare(b.name); return sortVal(b, key) - sortVal(a, key) || b.total - a.total || a.name.localeCompare(b.name); });
    var labels = view === "crit" ? CRIT : DEPT;
    var html = arr.map(function (s) {
      var vals = view === "crit" ? s.crit : s.dept;
      return '<li><button type="button" data-s="' + esc(s.name) + '" aria-pressed="' + (s.name === selected) + '"><span class="nm">' + esc(s.name) + '</span>' +
        '<span class="bar" style="width:' + (s.total / maxTotal * 100).toFixed(2) + '%">' + stackHTML(vals, labels, s.name).replace(/<i /g, '<i ') + '</span>' +
        '<span class="tot">' + (key[0] === "c" || key[0] === "d" ? sortVal(s, key) + '<span style="color:var(--muted)">/' + s.total + '</span>' : s.total) + '</span></button></li>';
    }).join("");
    $("#rows").innerHTML = html || '<li class="empty">No state matches “' + esc(q) + '”.</li>';
  }
  function rankOf(s) { return 1 + list.filter(function (o) { return o.total > s.total; }).length; }
  function ord(n) { var v = n % 100; if (v >= 11 && v <= 13) return n + "th"; return n + ({ 1: "st", 2: "nd", 3: "rd" }[n % 10] || "th"); }
  function renderCard() {
    var s = states[selected]; if (!s) return;
    var r = rankOf(s), tied = list.filter(function (o) { return o.total === s.total; }).length > 1;
    function bk(title, vals, labels) {
      var mx = Math.max.apply(null, vals.concat([1]));
      return '<table class="bk"><caption>' + title + '</caption><tbody>' + vals.map(function (v, i) {
        return '<tr><td><span class="sw" style="background:' + COL[i] + '"></span>' + esc(labels[i]) + '</td><td><span class="mini" style="width:' + (v / mx * 100) + '%;background:' + COL[i] + '"></span></td><td class="v">' + v + '</td></tr>';
      }).join("") + '</tbody></table>';
    }
    var bonus = [];
    if (s.crit[2]) bonus.push("GDP per capita (+" + s.crit[2] + ")");
    if (s.crit[3]) bonus.push("education (+" + s.crit[3] + ")");
    if (s.crit[4]) bonus.push("historical significance (+" + s.crit[4] + ")");
    if (s.crit[5]) bonus.push("low population (+" + s.crit[5] + ")");
    $("#stateCard").innerHTML = '<h3>' + esc(s.name) + '</h3>' +
      '<div class="big-num"><b>' + s.total + '</b><span>of ' + grand + ' seats · ' + (s.total / grand * 100).toFixed(1) + '%</span></div>' +
      '<p class="meta">' + (tied ? "Tied for " : "Ranks ") + ord(r) + ' of ' + list.length + '. ' + (bonus.length ? "Extra seats for " + bonus.join(", ") + "." : "Seats come from population and GDP only.") + '</p>' +
      bk("Where the seats come from", s.crit, CRIT) + bk("How they split by department", s.dept, DEPT) +
      '<a class="cite" href="' + A.s1 + '">First Schedule</a> · <a class="cite" href="' + A.s2 + '">Second Schedule</a>';
  }
  $("#rows").addEventListener("click", function (e) { var b = e.target.closest("button[data-s]"); if (!b) return; selected = b.getAttribute("data-s"); renderRows(); renderCard(); });
  $("#stateSearch").addEventListener("input", function () {
    renderRows();
    var first = $("#rows button[data-s]");

  });

  renderRows(); renderCard();

  /* tooltip */
  var tip = $("#tip");
  document.addEventListener("pointermove", function (e) {
    var t = e.target.closest && e.target.closest("[data-tip]");
    if (!t || e.pointerType === "touch") { tip.hidden = true; return; }
    tip.textContent = t.getAttribute("data-tip"); tip.hidden = false;
    var x = e.clientX + 14, y = e.clientY + 16, w = tip.offsetWidth, h = tip.offsetHeight;
    if (x + w > window.innerWidth - 8) x = e.clientX - w - 14;
    if (y + h > window.innerHeight - 8) y = e.clientY - h - 12;
    tip.style.left = x + "px"; tip.style.top = y + "px";
  });
  document.addEventListener("scroll", function () { tip.hidden = true; }, { passive: true });

  /* ---------- charter reader ---------- */
  var charter = $("#charterText");
  var heads = $$("h2", charter);

  $("#jump").addEventListener("change", function () { var id = this.value; if (id) { var el = document.getElementById(id); if (el) go(el, { smooth: true }); this.value = ""; } });
  var tocLinks = $$("#tocList a");
  function setActive() {
    var off = 140, idx = 0;
    for (var i = 0; i < heads.length; i++) { if (heads[i].getBoundingClientRect().top - off <= 0) idx = i; }
    tocLinks.forEach(function (a, i) { a.classList.toggle("active", i === idx); });
    var r = charter.getBoundingClientRect(), vh = window.innerHeight;
    var p = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (vh - r.top) / (r.height + vh * 0.2)));
    if (r.top > vh) p = 0;
    $("#pctBar").style.width = Math.round(p * 100) + "%";
    $("#pctText").textContent = Math.round(p * 100) + "% read";
    var onCharter = !charter.closest("[data-page]").hidden, sp = onCharter ? -r.top / Math.max(1, r.height - vh) : 0;
    $("#progress").style.transform = "scaleX(" + Math.max(0, Math.min(1, sp)) + ")";
    $("#progress").parentNode.style.opacity = onCharter ? "1" : "0";
  }
  window.addEventListener("scroll", setActive, { passive: true });
  window.addEventListener("resize", setActive);
  setActive();


  /* search */
  var units = $$("p, li, h3", charter).map(function (el) {
    var sec = el.closest("section"), h = sec ? sec.querySelector("h2") : null;
    return { el: el, text: el.textContent.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim(), where: h ? h.textContent : "" };
  });
  var resultsEl = $("#results"), countEl = $("#qCount");
  function snippet(text, q) {
    var i = text.toLowerCase().indexOf(q), start = Math.max(0, i - 70), end = Math.min(text.length, i + q.length + 110);
    var s = (start > 0 ? "…" : "") + text.slice(start, end) + (end < text.length ? "…" : "");
    var re = new RegExp(q.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&"), "gi");
    return esc(s).replace(re, function (m) { return "<mark>" + m + "</mark>"; });
  }
  var hits = [];
  $("#q").addEventListener("input", function () {
    var q = this.value.trim().toLowerCase();
    if (q.length < 2) { resultsEl.hidden = true; resultsEl.innerHTML = ""; countEl.textContent = ""; return; }
    hits = units.filter(function (u) { return u.text.toLowerCase().indexOf(q) !== -1; });
    countEl.textContent = hits.length + (hits.length === 1 ? " match" : " matches");
    resultsEl.hidden = false;
    resultsEl.innerHTML = hits.length ? hits.slice(0, 40).map(function (u, i) {
      return '<li><button type="button" data-h="' + i + '"><span class="where">' + esc(u.where) + '</span>' + snippet(u.text, q) + '</button></li>';
    }).join("") + (hits.length > 40 ? '<li class="empty">Showing the first 40. Add a word to narrow it down.</li>' : "") : '<li class="empty">No passages mention “' + esc(q) + '”. Try a shorter word.</li>';
  });
  resultsEl.addEventListener("click", function (e) {
    var b = e.target.closest("button[data-h]"); if (!b) return;
    var u = hits[+b.getAttribute("data-h")]; if (!u) return;
    go(u.el, { smooth: true, center: true });
    u.el.classList.remove("flash"); void u.el.offsetWidth; u.el.classList.add("flash");
  });

  $("#qGo").addEventListener("click", function () { $("#q").dispatchEvent(new Event("input")); });
  $("#q").addEventListener("keydown", function (e) { if (e.key === "Enter") { e.preventDefault(); var f = $("#results button"); if (f) f.focus(); } });

  /* ---------- faq ---------- */
  var faqBtn = $("#faqAll");
  faqBtn.addEventListener("click", function () {
    var ds = $$(".faq details"), allOpen = ds.every(function (d) { return d.open; });
    ds.forEach(function (d) { d.open = !allOpen; });
    faqBtn.textContent = allOpen ? "Expand all" : "Collapse all";
  });


  /* ---------- pages ---------- */
  var PAGES = { "home": "ChangeinBureauUS", "proposal": "The Proposal", "foundations": "Foundations", "how-it-works": "How It Works", "representation": "Representation", "charter": "The Charter", "faq": "FAQ", "about": "About" };
  var menuBtn = $("#menuBtn"), nav = $("#siteNav");
  function closeMenu() { nav.setAttribute("data-open", "false"); menuBtn.setAttribute("aria-expanded", "false"); }
  menuBtn.addEventListener("click", function () {
    var open = nav.getAttribute("data-open") === "true";
    nav.setAttribute("data-open", open ? "false" : "true");
    menuBtn.setAttribute("aria-expanded", open ? "false" : "true");
  });
  var current = null;
  function show(name, target) {
    var changed = name !== current;
    if (changed) {
      $$("[data-page]").forEach(function (p) { p.hidden = p.getAttribute("data-page") !== name; });
      $$("#siteNav a").forEach(function (a) { if (a.getAttribute("href") === "#" + name && !a.hasAttribute("data-focus-search")) a.setAttribute("aria-current", "page"); else a.removeAttribute("aria-current"); });
      document.title = name === "home" ? "ChangeinBureauUS" : PAGES[name] + " | ChangeinBureauUS";
      current = name;
    }
    closeMenu();
    if (target) {
      requestAnimationFrame(function () { go(target, { smooth: !changed }); if (target.matches("p, li, h2, h3")) { target.classList.remove("flash"); void target.offsetWidth; target.classList.add("flash"); } });
    } else {
      go(0, {});
    }
    setActive();
  }
  function route() {
    var h = "";
    try { h = decodeURIComponent(location.hash.slice(1)); } catch (e) { h = location.hash.slice(1); }
    if (!h) return show("home");
    if (PAGES.hasOwnProperty(h)) return show(h);
    var el = document.getElementById(h);
    if (el) { var p = el.closest("[data-page]"); if (p) return show(p.getAttribute("data-page"), el); }
    show("home");
  }
  window.addEventListener("hashchange", route);
  document.addEventListener("click", function (e) {
    var a = e.target.closest && e.target.closest('a[href^="#"]');
    if (!a) return;
    if (a.getAttribute("href") === location.hash) { e.preventDefault(); route(); }
    if (a.hasAttribute("data-focus-search")) setTimeout(function () { var q = $("#q"); if (q) { q.focus(); } }, 60);
  });
  $$("[data-top]").forEach(function (b) { b.addEventListener("click", function () { go(0, { smooth: true }); }); });
  $$("[data-scroll-next]").forEach(function (b) { b.addEventListener("click", function () { var n = document.getElementById("home-intro"); if (n) go(n, { smooth: true }); }); });
  /* ---------- motion: Lenis smooth scroll, reveals, hero parallax ---------- */
  var reduce = window.matchMedia && window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches;
  var lenis = null;
  if (false) { /* Lenis removed: native scrolling for reliable mouse-wheel support */
    try {
      $$(".rows, .sidenav-wrap, .results, .tablewrap, .nav").forEach(function (el) { el.setAttribute("data-lenis-prevent", ""); });
      lenis = new window.Lenis({ lerp: 0.08, wheelMultiplier: 1, smoothWheel: true, syncTouch: false });
      (function raf(t) { if (lenis) { lenis.raf(t); requestAnimationFrame(raf); } })(performance.now());
      var refit = function () { if (lenis) lenis.resize(); };
      window.addEventListener("load", refit);
      window.addEventListener("resize", refit);
      if ("ResizeObserver" in window) new ResizeObserver(refit).observe(document.body);
      /* safety net: if a mouse wheel turn does not move the page, fall back to normal scrolling */
      var checking = false;
      window.addEventListener("wheel", function (e) {
        if (!lenis || checking || Math.abs(e.deltaY) < 4 || e.target.closest("[data-lenis-prevent]")) return;
        var max = document.documentElement.scrollHeight - window.innerHeight;
        var y0 = window.scrollY;
        if ((e.deltaY > 0 && y0 >= max - 2) || (e.deltaY < 0 && y0 <= 2)) return;
        checking = true;
        setTimeout(function () {
          checking = false;
          if (lenis && Math.abs(window.scrollY - y0) < 1) { try { lenis.destroy(); } catch (x) {} lenis = null; document.documentElement.classList.remove("lenis", "lenis-smooth"); }
        }, 260);
      }, { passive: true });
    } catch (e) { lenis = null; }
  }
  function go(target, o) {
    o = o || {};
    var top = typeof target === "number";
    if (lenis) {
      lenis.resize();
      var off = top ? 0 : (o.center ? -(window.innerHeight / 2 - target.getBoundingClientRect().height / 2) : -24);
      lenis.scrollTo(target, { offset: off, immediate: !o.smooth, force: true });
      return;
    }
    var behavior = o.smooth && !reduce ? "smooth" : "auto";
    if (top) window.scrollTo({ top: target, behavior: behavior });
    else target.scrollIntoView({ behavior: behavior, block: o.center ? "center" : "start" });
  }
  if (!reduce && "IntersectionObserver" in window) {
    document.documentElement.classList.add("motion");
    var io = new IntersectionObserver(function (entries) {
      entries.forEach(function (en) { if (en.isIntersecting) { en.target.classList.add("in"); io.unobserve(en.target); } });
    }, { rootMargin: "0px 0px -8% 0px", threshold: 0.08 });
    $$("[data-page] .sec-head, [data-page] .col, [data-page] .align > div, [data-page] .path, [data-page] .stats3 > div, [data-page] .figure-text, [data-page] .portrait, [data-page] .split > div, [data-page] .reforms > div").forEach(function (el) {
      if (el.closest(".page-head, .hero")) return;
      var sib = el.parentNode ? Array.prototype.indexOf.call(el.parentNode.children, el) : 0;
      el.classList.add("rv");
      el.style.transitionDelay = Math.min(sib, 4) * 84 + "ms";
      io.observe(el);
    });
    var heroImg = $(".hero-img"), hero = $(".hero"), ticking = false;
    if (heroImg && hero) {
      window.addEventListener("scroll", function () {
        if (ticking) return;
        ticking = true;
        requestAnimationFrame(function () {
          ticking = false;
          if (current !== "home" || window.innerWidth <= 760) return;
          var y = window.scrollY || document.documentElement.scrollTop;
          if (y > hero.offsetHeight) return;
          heroImg.style.transform = "translate3d(0," + (y * 0.096).toFixed(1) + "px,0)";
        });
      }, { passive: true });
    }
  }
  route();
})();
</script>
